name: 46,XY Difference of Sex Development of Gynecological Interest

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Statement on Management of Differences of Sex Development

criteria.description: Presence of 46,XY karyotype with discordant gonadal or phenotypic sex
Evidence of gonadal dysgenesis or atypical gonadal development on histology or imaging
Abnormal androgen synthesis or action demonstrated by hormonal assays
Ambiguous genitalia or undervirilization in a 46,XY individual
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in sex development (e.g., SRY, AR, NR5A1)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of 46,XY karyotype with discordant gonadal or phenotypic sex plus evidence of gonadal dysgenesis or abnormal androgen synthesis/action
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including genetics, endocrinology, and gynecology.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes micropenis, hypospadias, or labioscrotal fusion abnormalities
Presence of streak gonads or dysgenetic testes

common.notes: Reduced penile size or incomplete labioscrotal fusion
Breast tissue development in phenotypic males

occasional.notes: Abnormal urethral opening on ventral penile shaft
Lack of secondary sexual characteristics development

rare.notes: Increased risk of gonadoblastoma or dysgerminoma

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric distress related to gender identity

rare.notes: Rare in cases with adrenal steroidogenesis defects
searchTerms: high blood pressure from adrenal gland problems

laboratory: Elevated luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)
Elevated anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) in some cases
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing absent or dysgenetic gonads
Müllerian structures presence or absence on pelvic imaging
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SRY, NR5A1, AR, or other sex development genes
other: Histopathology of gonadal tissue showing dysgenesis or streak gonads

distinguishingFeatures: Normal or elevated testosterone with end-organ resistance

redFlags: Primary amenorrhea in adolescent females with 46,XY karyotype
Rapidly enlarging gonadal mass suggestive of tumor
references: Hughes IA, et al. Consensus statement on management of intersex disorders. Arch Dis Child. 2006.
Lee PA, et al. Consensus statement on DSD. Pediatrics. 2006.
